# json

> JSON: parse text into a tree of values, read and build them, and write them back.

[source](../../registry/json.pkg) · truck

```
use std
use json

let ok = false
let doc = json_parse("{\"user\": {\"name\": \"Ada\", \"langs\": [\"en\", \"fr\"]}}", &ok)
if !ok
  print json_error()
  return 1
end
print json_as_str(json_path(doc, "user.name"))      // Ada
print json_len(json_path(doc, "user.langs"))        // 2

let reply = json_obj()
json_set(reply, "ok", json_bool(true))
json_set(reply, "count", json_int(2))
print json_write(reply)                             // {"ok":true,"count":2}
```

| package | gives |
|---|---|
| `json/value` | the `Json` tree: `json_obj`, `json_arr`, `json_str`, `json_int`, `json_set`, `json_push`, `json_get`, `json_at`, `json_path`, `json_as_int`, ... |
| `json/parse` | `json_parse(text, &ok)` and `json_error()` |
| `json/write` | `json_write(j)`, `json_pretty(j, indent)`, `json_quote(s)` |

Packenger has no floating point, so numbers keep their JSON text:
`json_as_int` truncates a fraction, `json_as_fixed(j, 2, &ok)` gives
hundredths, and writing a parsed number back gives exactly its text.

## Packages

| package | summary |
|---|---|
| [json/value](json/value.md) | JSON values: the Json tree, making values, and reading them. |
| [json/parse](json/parse.md) | Reading JSON: json_parse(text, &ok) gives the tree, or an error with its line and column. |
| [json/write](json/write.md) | Writing JSON: json_write for one line, json_pretty for indented output. |
